description:
(Summary from jobright.ai; the original posting may say more.)

Notion is building a collaborative AI workspace that brings knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools together. The Software Engineer, Mobile Core (Android) will build and improve the native Android foundation, including page rendering, editing, navigation, Home, Search, and Inbox, while optimizing performance and reliability. The role partners with product and design teams, uses AI development tools, and owns core product areas from concept through launch.
Android software engineer building core productivity app experiences and improving offline reliability, responsiveness, and performance

Responsibilities:
• Ship the core Notion experience on Android: Build and polish the surfaces people use every day—opening and reading pages, writing and editing, navigating the app, and the Home, Search, and Inbox tabs—on a native Kotlin and Jetpack Compose stack that is fast to open, smooth to scroll, and dependable offline
• Build with product and design, and iterate fast: Partner with product managers and designers to turn ideas into shipped features, then use feedback and data to make them better. Use AI coding tools and agents to build, test, and investigate faster, while you stay accountable for review, validation, and quality
• By the end of your first year, own a core product area: Take a core part of the Android app, like Home, Inbox, or a piece of the editor, from idea to launch, and shape it into an experience that helps people do their life’s work from their phone
• Make the app feel fast and reliable: Find and fix issues in startup time, scrolling, typing latency, crashes, and memory use across the surfaces you own, and add the tests and monitoring that catch regressions before users do

Requirements:
• You've built and shipped Android apps, through work, internships, or your own projects, and you're comfortable with modern Android—Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Coroutines/Flow, and Gradle
• You enjoy making UI feel fast and smooth, and you're curious about things like custom text rendering, complex lazy lists, or rich-text editing
• You care about how the app feels to use, not just how it works. You sweat the details of interactions and polish, and you use feedback and data to decide what to build next
• You build a clear picture of the problem before jumping to a fix, you can explain trade-offs in writing, and you ask for help early when you're stuck
• You use AI tools and agents as real collaborators, framing tasks clearly, reviewing generated changes, testing behavior, and designing workflows that make the broader team more effective

Preferred:
• Experience with a large, modular codebase is a plus
• Experience with performance profiling, realtime collaboration, or offline sync is a plus
• Experience moving a hybrid or web-based surface to native, or building something from 0→1, is a plus
• Web experience (TypeScript, React, Node) is welcome but not required
